dataset: Sample QA pairs for RAG evaluation
description: 20-30 question and expected answer pairs for evaluating RAG pipeline quality

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the RAG system described in this document?
questions.expected_answer: The main purpose of the RAG system is to answer questions based on uploaded documents using advanced retrieval techniques including multi-query generation, hybrid search (dense + sparse vectors), cross-encoder re-ranking, and relevance grading.
context_snippets: The system uses Qdrant for vector storage
It implements Phase 1-4 of the RAG pipeline

questions.question: Which embedding model is used for generating dense vectors?
questions.expected_answer: The system uses Google's text-embedding-004 model for generating dense vectors with 768 dimensions.

questions.question: What is the chunking strategy used for document ingestion?
questions.expected_answer: The system uses sentence-window chunking with 2-sentence child chunks indexed in Qdrant and a 5-sentence window for parent context sent to the LLM.

questions.question: Which LLM is used for chat operations?
questions.expected_answer: The system uses Groq's llama-3.3-70b-versatile model for chat operations with a temperature of 0.1 and max tokens of 1200.

questions.question: What database is used for vector storage?
questions.expected_answer: The system uses Qdrant as the vector database for storing both dense and sparse vectors with hybrid search support.

questions.question: How does the multi-query generation work?
questions.expected_answer: The multi-query generation uses the LLM to rewrite a single user question into 3 different phrasings, then runs hybrid retrieval for each phrasing and merges results using RRF.

questions.question: What is RRF and how is it used in this system?
questions.expected_answer: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) is a technique that merges multiple result sets by assigning scores based on reciprocal ranks. In this system, it's used to combine dense and sparse search results across all query variants.

questions.question: How does the CrossEncoder re-ranking work?
questions.expected_answer: The CrossEncoder reads query + chunk pairs together (not independently) and scores their relevance. It takes top-20 candidates after initial retrieval and returns top-5 after re-ranking.

questions.question: What is the fallback strategy when no relevant chunks are found?
questions.expected_answer: When no chunks pass the relevance threshold during grading, the system returns 'I could not find that in the uploaded document.' to prevent hallucinations.

questions.question: How does the context compression work?
questions.expected_answer: Context compression uses the LLM to read each chunk and extract only sentences relevant to the question, creating a smaller, cleaner context window for better answers and fewer tokens.

questions.question: What is the hallucination grader and how does it work?
questions.expected_answer: The hallucination grader is a LLM-based check that validates if an answer is fully grounded in the provided source chunks, returning grounded/not grounded with confidence scores.

questions.question: What format does the PDF parsing support?
questions.expected_answer: The system supports PDF and .txt file formats for upload. For PDFs, it uses unpdf to extract text content with per-page metadata.

questions.question: What is the parent-child chunking pattern?
questions.expected_answer: The parent-child pattern indexes small child chunks (2 sentences) in Qdrant but sends larger parent windows (5 sentences) to the LLM at generation time for richer context.

questions.question: How are sparse vectors built in this system?
questions.expected_answer: Sparse vectors use a TF-normalized BM25 approximation with stable hashing for terms. They are built alongside dense vectors in the same Qdrant collection for hybrid search.

questions.question: What is the batch size for upserting chunks to Qdrant?
questions.expected_answer: The system upserts chunks to Qdrant in batches of 100 for efficient indexing.

questions.question: What framework is used for the frontend?
questions.expected_answer: The frontend uses Next.js 15 with the App Router pattern and TypeScript for type safety.

questions.question: Where are the API routes located in this project?
questions.expected_answer: The API routes are located in the app/api directory with upload/route.ts for ingestion and ask/route.ts for querying.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the RAGAS metrics in Phase 4?
questions.expected_answer: The RAGAS metrics measure pipeline quality by evaluating context precision, context recall, faithfulness, and answer relevancy with real scores.

questions.question: How does the LLM-as-judge scoring work?
questions.expected_answer: The LLM-as-judge scoring uses Groq for fast, cheap scoring with structured Zod output, providing relevance scores (0-1) per chunk and faithfulness scores (0-1) per answer.

questions.question: What endpoint is used for evaluation in Phase 4?
questions.expected_answer: The POST /api/evaluate endpoint takes question, answer, and chunks as input and returns evaluation scores.

questions.question: Where is the eval dashboard located?
questions.expected_answer: The eval dashboard is located at app/eval/page.tsx and displays a table of questions with per-row scores and summary statistics.

questions.question: What metrics are tracked in the eval dashboard?
questions.expected_answer: The eval dashboard tracks average faithfulness, average context precision, and average answer relevancy to compare scores before and after phase upgrades.

questions.question: What is the data flow for the query pipeline after all phases?
questions.expected_answer: Question → generateQueryVariants (Phase 2) → hybrid retrieval per variant (Phase 1) → ragFusion RRF merge (Phase 2) → rerank CrossEncoder (Phase 2) → gradeChunks relevance filter (Phase 3) → compressContext (Phase 3) → generateGroundedAnswer (Phase 1) → gradeAnswer hallucination check (Phase 3) → Response

questions.question: What is the role of the grading threshold in Phase 3?
questions.expected_answer: The grading threshold (0.5 confidence score) filters out chunks below relevance threshold before generation, preventing low-quality context from affecting answer quality.

questions.question: How does the system handle scanned PDFs?
questions.expected_answer: The system throws an error 'No readable text found in the PDF. It may be a scanned image-only PDF.' when a scanned PDF without OCR text is detected.

metadata.format: JSON for testing RAG pipeline quality
